title: Implement QR-based Fire Extinguisher Certificate Management, Verification Pages, and PDF Downloads

requirements.text: Add backend data model and CRUD APIs for Fire Extinguisher Service Certificates, including all admin-entered fields: client/customer name, client address/location (optional), fire extinguisher type, capacity, cylinder manufacturing date, installation date, refilling date, next due date, refilling done by (technician name), tested by, certified by, refilling company name, remarks (optional), and an auto-generated unique certificate number.

quotes: Develop a QR-based digital certification system...
After login, the following fields should be available for data entry: ... Unique Certificate Number (Auto-generated)

acceptanceCriteria: Backend exposes typed methods to create, update, and fetch certificate records.
Certificate number is generated by the backend and returned as part of the stored record.
Optional fields (client address/location, remarks) are stored as optionals and can be omitted without errors.
Existing contact inquiry endpoints continue to function unchanged.

requirements.text: Implement admin-only authorization for certificate creation and editing using Internet Identity principals, ensuring customers/public users have view-only access.

quotes: An Admin / Authorized User login must be provided.
Certificate details must be editable only by Admin. Customers can view only, no editing.

acceptanceCriteria: Backend rejects create/update/admin-list operations for non-admin callers with a clear error.
Backend allows public read access for a single certificate verification lookup endpoint.
Admin set/management approach is defined and implemented (e.g., initial admin bootstrap and ability to manage admin principals) without relying on third-party auth providers.

requirements.text: Generate a unique, non-guessable public verification token per certificate and provide a public lookup API keyed by that token to support URLs like /certificate/<token>.

quotes: Certificate URLs must be secure and non-guessable

acceptanceCriteria: Every created certificate record includes a unique public token separate from the human-readable certificate number.
Public verification API only accepts the token and returns the associated record (or not found).
Tokens are not sequential/predictable (no simple counters exposed in the URL token).

requirements.text: Create a public Certificate Verification page route at /certificate/$token that fetches certificate details from the backend and renders the specified layout sections and labels in English, including validity status (Valid/Expired) and a clear warning when expired: “⚠️ Refilling Due – Please Contact Authorized Service Provider”.

quotes: When the QR code is scanned, a public-facing page should open displaying the following:
If validity expires, display a warning message: “⚠️ Refilling Due – Please Contact Authorized Service Provider”

acceptanceCriteria: Navigating directly to /certificate/<token> renders a complete certificate view when the token exists.
If the token does not exist, the page shows a not-found state (no crash).
Validity is computed from Next Due Date vs current date and displayed as Valid or Expired.
When Expired, the specified warning text is displayed prominently.
Page includes: company logo, company name, tagline text, client info, service info, technical details, authorization details, footer text, certificate number, and a small QR display.

requirements.text: Create an Admin UI (protected by Internet Identity login) to create, edit, and list certificates, with a data entry form containing all fields specified by the user and automatic QR generation after saving.

quotes: An Admin / Authorized User login must be provided. After login, the following fields should be available for data entry: ...
After saving the data, the system must automatically generate a unique QR Code for that record.

acceptanceCriteria: Admin area is accessible via a dedicated route (e.g., /admin/certificates) and prompts login when not authenticated.
Non-admin authenticated users are blocked from admin functions with a clear message.
Admin can create a new certificate record and is shown the generated certificate number and public verification URL token after save.
Admin can edit an existing certificate and changes persist.
Admin can see a list/table of certificates with at least certificate number, client name, next due date, and a link to the public verification page.

requirements.text: Implement QR code rendering on the frontend that encodes the public verification URL for the certificate (using the app’s deployed origin plus /certificate/<token>), and display it both on the admin certificate view and on the public verification page (small display).

quotes: Each fire extinguisher must have a unique QR code
On scanning the QR code, it should open a secure public verification page on our website

acceptanceCriteria: QR code is generated from the canonical verification URL and updates correctly per certificate.
QR code is visible in the public certificate verification page and in the admin certificate view/download area.
QR code is scannable from the screen in common mobile camera apps and resolves to the same certificate page.

requirements.text: Add “Download PDF” capability for admins to generate an A4, print-ready certificate PDF that includes all entered details, company branding (logo/name/tagline), certificate number, and the QR code.

quotes: Admin should have an option to download a PDF certificate
PDF should be A4 size and print-ready
PDF must include: All entered details, QR Code, Company branding, Signature / stamp

acceptanceCriteria: Admin can click “Download PDF” for a certificate and receives a generated PDF file.
The PDF is A4-sized and contains all fields shown on the public verification page plus certificate number and QR code.
PDF includes the existing static logo asset from frontend/public/assets/generated/shree-fire-works-logo.dim_512x512.png.
PDF generation works client-side without requiring external services.

requirements.text: Add backend persistence for certificate records with upgrade-safe stable storage; introduce a conditional backend migration to preserve existing stored data (e.g., contact inquiries) while adding certificate storage.

quotes: Develop a QR-based digital certification system...

acceptanceCriteria: Certificate records persist across canister upgrades.
Existing inquiries data (if any) is preserved across upgrades.
A migration file is added/updated only as needed to safely evolve stable state (no unnecessary migration if not required).

constraints: Backend must remain a single Motoko actor in backend/main.mo (no additional backend services).

Do not edit frontend immutable paths: frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts, frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.tsx, frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts, frontend/src/main.tsx, frontend/src/components/ui.
Use Internet Identity for authentication (no third-party auth providers).
Generated/static images must be served from frontend/public/assets/generated (do not proxy images through the backend).
nonGoals: Search certificates by certificate number or client name.
Multiple user roles beyond admin vs public viewing.
